title: Teachers Aide Salary Guide: Award Rates, Tax, and Super in Australia
description: Find out the typical teachers aide salary under the Schools General Staff Award, including hourly rates, fortnightly pay, tax, and superannuation.
salarySummary: A full-time teachers aide at the minimum award level earns $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a teachers aide in Australia?
faqs.a: The minimum hourly rate for a teachers aide covered by the Educational Services (Schools) General Staff Award is $26.44 per hour for a Level 1.1 full-time employee working 38 ordinary hours per week. This matches the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026. Higher classifications (Level 2 and above) attract higher rates. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: Do teachers aides get casual loading?
faqs.a: Yes. Under the Schools General Staff Award, casual teachers aides are paid a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a Level 1.1 employee, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements such as annual leave and sick leave.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for teachers aides?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The Super Guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For a full-time teachers aide earning $1,004.90 per week, the employer contributes an extra $120.59 per week into super. This is not deducted from your pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Teachers Aide Salary

A teachers aide (also called an education assistant or teacher assistant) supports classroom teachers in schools and early childhood services. Your pay is most likely covered by the **Educational Services (Schools) General Staff Award 2020**, which sets minimum wages for non-teaching staff. This guide explains how to convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, and what tax and super you can expect.

## How to Calculate Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

The standard formula for annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a full-time employee works **38 ordinary hours per week**, as defined in the award. For example, a teachers aide at the minimum award level (Level 1.1) earns $26.44 per hour. Their annual pay is:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44

If you work part-time, adjust the hours accordingly. The same formula applies: multiply your hourly rate by your actual weekly hours, then by 52. For a casual employee, use the casual rate (including the 25% loading) and the same hours assumption.

## Award Rates for Teachers Aides

The Schools General Staff Award has multiple classification levels. The most common entry point for a teachers aide is **Level 1** or **Level 2**. Here are the minimum weekly and hourly rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guide (effective from 1 July 2026):

| Classification | Weekly rate (38 hours) | Hourly rate |
|----------------|------------------------|-------------|
| Level 1.1 | $1,004.90 | $26.44 |
| Level 1.2 | $1,029.10 | $27.08 |
| Level 2.1 | $1,073.10 | $28.24 |
| Level 2.2 | $1,106.20 | $29.11 |

Higher levels (3–8) apply to more experienced or specialised roles. Your actual pay may be above the minimum if your employer offers a higher rate or if an enterprise agreement applies.

### Casual Loading

Casual teachers aides receive a **25% loading** on the minimum hourly rate. For Level 1.1, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. This loading is paid instead of entitlements like annual leave, sick leave, and public holiday pay. When using the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) tool, do not add the loading yourself; the checkbox applies it automatically.

## Fortnightly Pay

Most teachers aides are paid fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly rate by 2. For a Level 1.1 full-time employee:

$1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight

This is before tax and any deductions. If you are paid monthly, divide your annual salary by 12.

## Tax on Your Teachers Aide Salary

Australia uses a progressive tax system. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% for each dollar over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% for each dollar over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% for each dollar over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: 45% for each dollar over $190,000

Plus a **Medicare levy** of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). The tax-free threshold means you pay no tax on the first $18,200. For a teachers aide earning $52,269 per year, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be around $7,800, leaving a take-home pay of about $44,500. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

## Superannuation (Super)

Your employer must pay **Super Guarantee** contributions of **12%** of your ordinary time earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay. The contributions are capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For a full-time teachers aide earning $1,004.90 per week, the super contribution is:

$1,004.90 × 12% = $120.59 per week

Over a year, that adds about $6,270 to your retirement savings. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

## Comparing to Other Roles

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, which is the same as the Level 1.1 teachers aide rate. However, many teachers aides progress to higher levels. The **ABS Average Weekly Earnings** (May 2026) for full-time adult ordinary time earnings is $2,083.70 per week, which is well above the award minimum. Teachers aide salaries are typically below this average, reflecting the support role.

## Important Notes

- The calculations here assume you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.
- If you work in a long day care centre, different rates may apply under the Teachers Award – but that award is for qualified teachers, not aides.
- Always check your actual pay against the award or your enterprise agreement. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides a [pay guide](/blog) and a [reference table](/data) for all awards.

## Summary

A teachers aide salary starts at $26.44 per hour (or $33.05 casual) under the Schools General Staff Award. Annual gross pay for a full-time employee is about $52,269. After tax and Medicare, take-home pay is roughly $44,500, plus super of around $6,270 paid on top. Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to calculate your own figures, and remember that award rates are minimums – you may earn more.
